html:
The Tecuexe were an Indigenous people of western Mexico, around what is now Guadalajara in Jalisco. Little is known of their language or customs beyond Spanish accounts.

They lived in farming towns in the valleys and canyons near the Río Grande de Santiago, next to peoples such as the Caxcanes. Spanish conquest came in 1530 with the brutal campaign of Nuño Beltrán de Guzmán. The Tecuexe joined the great rising of the Mixtón War in 1540 to 1542, which nearly drove the Spanish from the region. After its defeat they were absorbed into New Spain and faded as a separate people.
